title: Marine Corps Strategist (I) (LtCol to Maj) FMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
6.     MOS 0509, Marine Corps Strategist (I) (LtCol to Maj) FMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Marine Corps Strategists are strategic leaders that support
senior military and civilian leader decision-making at service, combatant
command, departmental, and national levels. They also understand and
represent Marine Corps interests in the joint and national strategy
formulation processes, aid senior leaders in shaping national, defense, and
military strategic guidance, and anticipate how strategic guidance will
evolve in near, mid, and long-term. As uniformed officers with doctorate
level education in national security-specific areas (e.g., strategy,
international relations, military history, political science), these Marines
provide senior leaders with advanced research, writing, conceptual framing,
quantitative and qualitative data analysis, and planning for all forms of
strategic engagement and communication. At all levels, they are well-suited
to help generate national, defense, military, and service strategies designed


                                          1-33                          Enclosure (1)
 1108                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



to address current and future operational challenges. Marine Corps
Strategists will reside at the Headquarters Marine Corps, combatant command,
joint staff, and OSD levels. 0509 billets are listed as additional skills
designators and maintained by DC PP&O and DC M&RA to ensure appropriate
billets are staffed with Marine Corps Strategist.

       b.   Prerequisites

        (1) Meet eligibility requirements for the PhDP Strategist Track as
laid out in ref (C).

        (2) Officers must be selected for the PhDP Strategist program to be
eligible for this MOS.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) PhDP Strategists must complete all university PhD program
requirements to include defense, approval, and submission of their
dissertation.

        (2) This MOS will be assigned to a Marine in an appropriate service,
joint, or OSD planning billet by submitting a graduation certificate through
the Marine’s servicing IPAC.

    d. Duties. Lead research and planning efforts for major commands and
DCs. Represent the USMC (service and operating forces) in strategy
formulation at the joint and national level. Conduct complex problem framing
to understand existing and anticipate future strategic guidance; ensure
campaign planning efforts at service and OPFOR level are appropriately
nested.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
